ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two students are carrying out basketball passing-and-catching training in physical education class. Student Jia throws the basketball from point A to Yi (the trajectory of the basketball's motion is shown as solid line 1 in the figure), and Yi catches it at point B and then passes the basketball back to Jia (the trajectory of the basketball's motion is shown as dashed line 2 in the figure). It is known that the maximum heights of the basketball's motion in the air are exactly the same. If air resistance is ignored, then which of the following statements is correct ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The power of the work done by gravity at the instant before the basketball falls to point B is equal to the power of the work done by gravity at the instant before it falls to point C (which is at the same height as points A and B)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the lower left of the figure, point A is marked; in the lower right, point B is marked; and in the lower middle-left, point C is marked. The three points are located near the same horizontal height. Solid-line trajectory 1 is a parabola, rising from point A to the highest point and then descending to point B. Dashed-line trajectory 2 is also a parabola, rising from near point B and then descending to point C. The highest points of the two trajectories in the figure are at the same horizontal height, consistent with the statement in the question that the maximum heights of the basketball's motion in the air are exactly the same. Reasoning: After air resistance is ignored, the basketball is subject only to gravity in the air. Comparing the instant before the basketball falls to point B and the instant before it falls to point C, the two motions can both be regarded as the basketball falling vertically from their respective highest points to the same height. At the highest point, the vertical component of velocity is 0 in both cases; the highest heights of the two trajectories are the same, and B and C are also at the same height as A, so the vertical falling height from the highest point to point B and from the highest point to point C is the same. From the relation of motion in the vertical direction, it can be known that the magnitudes of the vertical components of velocity before reaching the same height in the two cases are the same, and the directions are both downward. The instantaneous power of the work done by gravity is P=F重·v, and is related only to the downward vertical component of velocity; horizontal velocity does not affect the power of gravity. Therefore, the powers of the work done by gravity at the two instants are equal, namely P_B=P_C.
